# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

founder.order_why: It runs the way I'd explain Fresco myself: the superintendents and their end-of-day trailer time first, then the daily-log problem, then the narrated-video scribe and how it fits Procore and ACC, and only then the pilot and who to ask.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.') on either side of the recall-window screen, so the context step reads as if it is asked twice, even if the second is only the rest of the fields.
founder.missing: Nothing asks who pays or what it costs. The general contractor pays per site, the buyer is someone like the operations lead or CFO, and the price is about $1k per site per month (less on multi-site or multi-month terms), set against the 1.5 to 3 hours a day superintendents spend now. The flow also has no relative-advantage belief to choose (screen 14 goes to a check but no 'what do you believe' screen, unlike compatibility and adoption friction).

PRIMARY.order_why: Screen 4 asks whether I could talk over the site noise before screen 6 even tells me Fresco means talking over videos on my walk, so it should come after 6.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 4 and 6 both ask whether I'd talk on my walks for Fresco, once about the noise and once about doing it at all.
PRIMARY.missing: Nobody asked how I do the log now or how long it takes me, like the hours I spend uploading photos to Procore at the end of the day, or whether I've needed the log to back me up in a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why7: The rows have the card's shape (1 to 4 benefits, under 9 words, the lead kept), but the Keel-will-test box keeps only the first benefit while the belief joins both with 'and', which is the card's top pitfall, and the intro says strangers will tick from my benefits, which the card forbids showing them.
screens.instead: Rows: 'Notes done during the walk, not after' · 'Hours back at the end of the day' · 'Action items to the crew the same day'; intro: 'Strangers will only be asked if Fresco would have done their last daily log better, a lot, a little, no difference or worse; these rows are your belief, not their options'; and the Keel-will-test box showing every kept benefit joined with 'and'.

screens.why1: Right after what it does better, asking what my supers have to do to start using Fresco is the obvious next question, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: Setup, extra steps, learning: plain to me, and the answer I typed reads in a super's own words.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super has to do to use Fresco: shoot narrated clips on the walk and check the notes before they go to the crew or Procore.
screens.why4: The only chip is the escape, Leave this out of the study, which fits a founder who can't say what the effort is.
screens.why5: The belief keeps my first effort word for word, and the second stays on my list as I typed it.
screens.why7: Both efforts are steps the super takes himself, are at most 9 words each, are in my order, and touch neither Compatibility nor Purchase friction; the belief is my first one, so a stranger's Yes or No answers it, and the founder's escape is there.

screens.why1: After I typed what supers would have to do to start, it makes sense for Keel to show me its list of those steps to check before I pick one to test.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them on walks, the notes, and Procore or ACC are all how my supers and I talk, though the intro repeats the title word for word.
screens.why3: Each row is something a super would know from their own day: walking the site with a phone, signing off the notes, logging into Procore.
screens.why4: The first two rows are good, distinct efforts, but 'Connect their Procore or ACC account once' is about fitting the tools they already use, which I answered two screens back, and on most of our jobs the GC's Procore admin does it, not the super.
screens.why5: Narrated short videos on the walk and pushing to Procore/ACC are my own mechanism, and checking the notes before they go out is a fair step I'd own.
screens.why7: The measure, the count of 1 to 4, the 'their' voice and the 9-word cap all hold, and a belief on the first row could be supported or refuted by yes/no, but the Procore row bends the card's rules: it repeats Compatibility's ground and is often another role's setup.
screens.instead: Keep 'Take short videos and talk over them on walks' and 'Check and fix the notes before they go out'; replace the Procore row with 'Say who and by when for each item on the walk'.

screens.why1: Right after I checked the efforts Keel wrote from my answer, picking the one most likely to stop a super is the obvious next step before the test.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them on walks, Procore or ACC: these are a super's own words, and the title reads clean on first pass.
screens.why3: I know my supers, and I know the narrated walk is the habit they would balk at, so I can pick from what I've seen on site.
screens.why4: Three distinct efforts, each one step, no two the same, and the one I'd pick, talking over videos on the walk, is there.
screens.why5: The rows are my efforts as I typed them, nothing reworded, and the belief is my picked row word for word.
screens.why7: The measure, shape, order, single pick and belief all fit the card, but 'Connect their Procore or ACC account once' leans on Compatibility's ground and is often done by the GC's Procore admin rather than the super, so one rule is bent.
screens.instead: Which one is most likely to stop them? · Take short videos and talk over them on site walks · Check and fix the notes before they go out · (drop the Procore/ACC connect row: Compatibility tests it)

screens.why1: Right before strangers see the study is the natural place to decide whether to ask the willing ones to try Fresco on a live job, and I want those names for a first site.
screens.why2: Pilot is my everyday word with general contractors, and the hint says exactly what line gets added and where I see the yeses.
screens.why3: Whether I want leads for a trial on one live job is my own call as the founder.
screens.why4: Yes or no is the whole choice, the two chips are distinct and plain, and no escape is needed for a decision only I make.
screens.why5: My commitment step is a paid pilot on one site bought by the contractor, but the line 'Would you try this for real? Leave your email' reads like a free personal sign-up and does not say whether supers or the ops leads get it.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? People who say yes get a line at the end: "Would you try this on one of your jobs? Leave your email." (asked of superintendents and contractor buyers alike) — Yes, ask them / No pilot

screens.why1: Choosing who asks the questions is an obvious last step before the link goes out to supers, right after deciding on the pilot offer.
screens.why2: It's mostly plain, but the hint says the interviewer asks 'on video' and then has me pick a 'voice', so I'd re-read it to work out whether I'm picking a face, a voice or both, and '400 credits' is Keel's word, not mine.
screens.why3: I know my supers get texts on site and in the trailer, so I can judge which voice they'd sit through.
screens.why4: Two named voices with a 5-second sample each are distinct and easy to pick from, but there's no 'text only, no voice' choice, even though the hint says people can read and type anyway.
screens.why5: This is Keel's own setup screen and nothing of what I typed about Fresco is reworded or lost.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? (They can always read and type instead.) — Daphne ▶ 5 s · Saskia ▶ 5 s · No voice, written questions only

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions, it's obvious I'd next pick how my supers take the interview before it goes out.
screens.why2: Plain words throughout -- talking, typing, tapping, a link -- nothing a founder of a scribe app would stumble on.
screens.why3: I know my supers are in a truck or trailer with a phone at day's end, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap through or talk to a video.
screens.why4: Three distinct modes plus a let-them-choose option cover the real choices, and no escape is needed for a setting I'm deciding myself.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product is altered here; it says superintendents, my word, and the choice I made (Read and tap) is offered as typed.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words: people I know by name, a list from a search, one open link posted where supers already are -- I read it once and know which I want.
screens.why3: I know exactly whose numbers I have -- the supers at the GCs we've been driving to in Napa and the South Bay -- so this is my own call to make.
screens.why4: The three ways are distinct and complete, but the middle one leans on a 'Contacts page' I haven't seen in this flow, so it reads a little odd at this point.
screens.why5: Nothing of what I typed is changed; my pick, people I know by name, is kept as I made it.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? -- Supers I know by name (one link each) / A list from a Keel search (one link each, you send them) / One open link I post where supers already gather (each signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside its deciding number on every card ('4 counted · 5 needed to call it'), so I know nothing is decided and why, though the head line oddly names only Compatibility as if it alone set the verdict.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart, only a tally line; it reads plainly as three beliefs, all too few to call, but '7 people answered' against '4 counted' needs a second look because the page never says why three of my superintendents were not counted.
screens.why_b3: The three dimension names and belief lines are the ones I checked, but the statement under the title garbles my product (it 'sends the notes to Procore or ACC in one click and gets back the notes ... in Procore or ACC'), and the Relative advantage card shows the two-part belief while Keel told me it would test only the hours-back part.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do next: not whether to get one more counted answer per belief, nor why three answers were set aside, nor whether to send the study to more superintendents.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond the data; n stays visible on every card and the low count is said plainly as too few to call.
screens.instead: None of the three beliefs can be called yet: 7 superintendents answered, but 3 were not counted (say why), leaving 4 where 5 are needed. Get at least one more counted answer on each before reading anything into the solution.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside "4 counted · 5 needed to call it", so I know there's no verdict and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the 5 answered / 4 counted are plain, but the strip's "your bar · 4 of 5" with the marker at 4 reads like 4 of 5 said yes and took me a second look to square with "no more than 1 in 3".
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and "Most superintendents could talk over the noise on site" are the name and line I checked, though the Asked and bar lines clip it to "Could talk over..." and "You said could talk..." with no subject.
screens.why_b4: "Ray's no is the one to ask about" is a real pointer, but it never says the plain next step, which is to get one more counted answer, ideally from a super on an active, loud job.
screens.why_b5: The lean is honestly hedged, but the question was pinned to "your last daily log" (done in the trailer) instead of the site walk where the noise is, and the closing quote about subs and crane wind isn't about talking over noise at all, so it reads as evidence it isn't.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 needed counted (3 could talk over the noise on their last site walk, Ray couldn't); get one more answer from a super on a loud active job, and ask Ray what drowned him out.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The chart plainly counts 3 'a lot better' and 1 'no difference' over 4, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with its marker at 4 reads like 4 of 5 people were for me; I had to look again to see it means the 5 needed to call it.
screens.why_b3: The belief line carries both my benefits, hours back and action items to the crew the same day, but the next line says 'You said hours back at the end of the day', and the Check told me only hours back would be tested, so I can't tell which belief this card is scoring.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would settle it, or that Denise's quote says her log isn't the pain.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, it says 'a small group: a lean, not a call' and that the question was a hypothetical, and it doesn't dress 3 of 4 up as a win.
screens.instead: Say 'Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted said a lot better, 1 said no difference; one more counted answer settles it. Testing hours back only, not action items to the crew', and label the strip's mark '5 needed to call'.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits with the number that decides it, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know why there's no verdict.
screens.why_b2: The bars clearly count answers over 5 people with 4 counted, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' beside a rule of 'no more than 1 in 3 against' and a marker at 4 took me a second look to work out where the bar actually sits.
screens.why_b3: The title Adoption friction and 'Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks' are the belief I checked on the way in, word for word.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me the lean is my way (1 against of 4, under the 1-in-3 line) or that one more superintendent's answer would let it call.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the small group is called a lean not a call, Luis's guess is set apart by name, and the 2 conditional yeses are split out from the 1 plain yes, so nothing is oversold.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted, 5 needed — so far it leans your way (3 for, 2 of them only if worth it; 1 against, under the 1-in-3 line); one more counted superintendent would settle it.

screens.why_b1: Both boxes say Too few to call and put the number that decides it right beside the verdict: 4 counted, 5 needed.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and Relative advantage carry my own belief lines word for word, though the Relative advantage line shows my full sentence with the crew action items, not the narrower hours-back line Keel actually tested.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what to do next, such as sending the study to more supers, or what one superintendent saying their log is already done means for the hours-back pitch.
screens.why_b5: Each box keeps n in view (4 counted, 1 against, 1 asked why), says it is too few to call, and makes no claim beyond those people.
screens.why_b6: Both quotes tell me something I didn't type: Denise finishes her log on the tablet before she leaves the gate, and both say the schedule and getting subs to show are what really eat the day, which challenges hours-back as my wedge.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5 needed); send the study to more superintendents. Both who said no named the schedule and no-show subs, not the log, as the real time sink, so test whether hours back on the log is the pain worth selling.

screens.why1: Asking first whether my jobs run on project software makes sense before anything about getting photos and notes into the daily log.
screens.why2: Every super knows what construction project management software means, since that's Procore or ACC to us, so I can answer it on first hearing.
screens.why3: I know exactly what my jobs run on because I'm in it every day.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it cleanly, and the gate has no escape, so nothing is missing.
screens.why5: Nothing about the founder's product or plan reaches me; it only asks what software my jobs use.
screens.why6: It's one short question with two options I can hold, though 'construction project management software' is a bit of a mouthful aloud.
screens.instead: Is any job you're running now set up in software like Procore or ACC? Yes; or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my job runs on Procore or similar, asking about my last week of daily logs is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log, site walk, photos and notes are my own words; I'd answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I do the daily log every day, so I know exactly what I did this week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing about any product or the company's plan reaches me; it's just my log.
screens.why6: One short question ending in 'Yes or no', easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Putting my photos and notes into the daily log is something every super does every day, so this asks the circumstance, not the problem; everyone says Yes, nobody can truly say No, and the belief can never be refuted.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you have to type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after asking whether I got my photos and notes into the daily log after the walk, showing me a tool for exactly that is an obvious next step.
screens.why2: Site walk, videos, notes, assignees, due dates, Procore and ACC are all words I use every day; 'AI scribe' is a little fancy, but I get it on first hearing.
screens.why3: It describes my own site walk, my crew's action items and the Procore log I fill in, so I can picture it against my own day.
screens.why4: A card to read, with no options or box.
screens.why5: The idea is shown on purpose as an 'Imagine' card, and nothing of the founder's plan or inside terms for people reaches me beyond the idea itself.
screens.why6: Heard once it's long: the last line re-lists the videos, the notes, Procore or ACC and one click that I just heard, instead of pointing back to it, so the belief is lost in the repeat.
screens.instead: Keep the first two paragraphs, and say the belief as: 'The people building it believe it would do all of that for you, so the log is done when the walk is.'

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, asking whether I could talk my notes over the site noise is the obvious next thing to ask about an AI scribe that listens to video.
screens.why2: The question is missing its subject, so 'Could talk over the noise on site?' needs a second read to work out it means could I have talked into my phone over the noise.
screens.why3: Tying it to my last daily log is off, since I write the log in the trailer at the end of the day and the noise is on the walk, so I'd have to guess which moment it means.
screens.why4: Yes easily, most of the time, only sometimes, no is a clean ability scale in words I'd use, and I can't tell fits as the one escape.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks past the card, but the condition drifted from speaking into my phone over the noise on my site walk to a clipped clause with no subject, no phone and the wrong occasion.
screens.why6: Said aloud the four options hold fine, but 'Could talk over the noise on site?' with no 'you' sounds broken and makes me stop to work out what is being asked.
screens.why7: The measure, the ability four, the balance and the escape all meet the card, but the occasion is bent: my last daily log is not the moment I would talk over the noise, so the could-you-have has a shaky true answer.
screens.instead: On your last site walk, could you have spoken into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, asking whether Fresco would have done my daily log better is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: I get it on one read, but nobody on my site says "keep an accurate record of the day's work" (we say "write up the daily"), and "AI scribe" is a phrase I'd never use.
screens.why3: I write a daily log every working day, so I can answer from my last one.
screens.why4: The four answers run from a lot better to worse, they don't overlap, and "I can't tell" fits when I haven't seen the thing work.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks past the idea card, but the job is in the founder's wording rather than mine, and "turns videos into notes" doesn't match how I work, since I take photos.
screens.why6: Heard aloud it's two long sentences that repeat Fresco's whole description, which is a mouthful before the four short options, though the options themselves say well.
screens.why7: The four fixed answers are in order with two for and two against, and the one escape is set apart, but the occasion is any last daily log rather than the hard one where the record mattered, like a delay dispute with the owner.
screens.instead: Think of the last daily log you had to get exactly right, like for a delay claim. Would Fresco have made that log better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after asking if Fresco would beat my daily log, it makes sense to ask whether I'd actually shoot the videos and talk over them on my walks.
screens.why2: Short videos and talking over them on a walk is plain to me; I walk the job with my phone out all day anyway.
screens.why3: I do the walks myself every day, so I know whether I'd narrate a clip between the GC trailer and the third floor.
screens.why4: The four cover it, but my real catch is noise and having my hands full near the work, not whether it is worth it, so that middle yes is close to a plain yes.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks past the idea card; it just says what I would do on my walks.
screens.why6: One short question and four short options I can hold after one hearing, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: The step is mine to take, every option answers whether I would take it, two count for and two against, and I can't tell sits apart as the card requires.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd take short videos and talk over them on your walks. Would you do that, or not? Yes; only if the noise and my hands allowed it; probably not; no; or I can't tell.
